regulations.title: PROBES, PROBE CABLE EXTENDERS AND PROBE COVERS
General - Probes, Probe Cable Extenders and Probe Covers
Labelling - Probes, Probe Cable Extenders and Probe Covers
Requirements applicable to all ME Equipment and ME systems

requirements.description: PROBES, PROBE CABLE EXTENDERS and PROBE COVERS comply with the requirements of this particular standard

MANUFACTURERS of PROBES, PROBE CABLE EXTENDERS and PROBE COVERS conduct tests to ensure that all CLINICAL THERMOMETER specifications are met with each MODEL OR TYPE REFERENCE of CLINICAL THERMOMETER with which they are intended to be used
All CLINICAL THERMOMETERS with which compatibility to the PROBES, PROBE CABLE EXTENDERS and PROBE COVERS is claimed are listed in the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT

It is the responsibility of the MANUFACTURER of a PROBE, PROBE CABLE EXTENDER and PROBE COVER, including a REPROCESSED PROBE, PROBE CABLE EXTENDER and PROBE COVER, to have their PROCESSES VALIDATED to ensure that any new or REPROCESSED product complies with the requirements of this particular standard
At least one MODEL OR TYPE REFERENCE of CLINICAL THERMOMETER is included in the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT provided with each PROBE, PROBE CABLE EXTENDER and PROBE COVER
ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT statement a): Designed for use with specific thermometer or monitoring equipment
ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT statement b): The OPERATOR is responsible for checking the compatibility of the thermometer or monitoring equipment, PROBE, PROBE CABLE EXTENDER AND PROBE COVER before use
ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT statement c): Incompatible components can result in degraded performance
Amendment: if applicable, attachment of ACCESSORIES as necessary to achieve the BASIC SAFETY and ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER
Amendment [add note to list element b]: the requirements of this document are not considered deviations or allowances

The following degradations, if associated with BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE, shall not be allowed: component failures; changes in programmable parameters or settings; reset to default settings; change of operating mode; change in LABORATORY ACCURACY at any point in the RATED OUTPUT RANGE and in the RATED EXTENDED OUTPUT RANGE greater than permitted in 201.101.2 without the generation of either a TECHNICAL ALARM CONDITION or an indication of abnormal operation

The CLINICAL THERMOMETER may exhibit temporary degradation of performance during IMMUNITY testing which does not require OPERATOR intervention and does not affect BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE
In the event of disruption during IMMUNITY tests, the CLINICAL THERMOMETER shall recover from any disruption within 30 s
PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION a): observing the OUTPUT TEMPERATURE
PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION b): properly positioning CLINICAL THERMOMETER or PROBE at the MEASURING SITE
PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION c): starting the CLINICAL THERMOMETER from power off
PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION d): turning off the CLINICAL THERMOMETER
PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION e): performing a basic pre-use functional check of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER
Optional PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION f): performing a basic pre-use functional check of the ALARM SIGNALS
Optional PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION g): configuring the ACCESSORIES including connection of the detachable parts to the CLINICAL THERMOMETER
Optional PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION h): REPROCESSING the ACCESSORIES

Optional PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTION i): setting the OPERATOR-adjustable controls: switching between MEASURING SITES; setting CLINICAL THERMOMETER control parameters; setting ALARM LIMITS; inactivating ALARM SIGNALS

tests.acceptance_criteria: Recovery from any disruption within 30 s

semantic_fragments.content: An ADJUSTED MODE CLINICAL THERMOMETER that makes continuous estimates of the REFERENCE BODY SITE temperature is exempt from the requirements of this subclause (N/E)

The following degradations, if associated with BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE, shall not be allowed during EMC/immunity testing: component failures; changes in programmable parameters or settings; reset to default settings; change of operating mode; change in LABORATORY ACCURACY at any point in the RATED OUTPUT RANGE and in the RATED EXTENDED OUTPUT RANGE greater than permitted in 201.101.2 without the generation of either a TECHNICAL ALARM CONDITION or an indication of abnormal operation.

The CLINICAL THERMOMETER may exhibit temporary degradation of performance (e.g. deviation from the performance indicated in the instructions for use during IMMUNITY testing), which does not require OPERATOR intervention and that does not affect BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE. In the event of disruption during IMMUNITY tests, the CLINICAL THERMOMETER shall recover from any disruption within 30 s.

For clause 206 Usability, IEC 60601-1-6:2010+A1:2013 applies except as specified. Optional PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTIONS f) through i) (alarm signal check, accessories configuration, accessories reprocessing, and operator-adjustable controls including measuring site switching, alarm limit setting and alarm signal inactivation) are marked N/A for this particular CLINICAL THERMOMETER.

It is the responsibility of the MANUFACTURER of a PROBE, PROBE CABLE EXTENDER and PROBE COVER, including a REPROCESSED PROBE, PROBE CABLE EXTENDER and PROBE COVER, to have their PROCESSES VALIDATED to ensure that any new or REPROCESSED product complies with the requirements of this particular standard.
